messages:
michelle: paging: GPU pool exhausted in us-west-2 (customer-facing routing degraded). queue length ~12k, token throttles spiking, many requests 429. Incident bot fired: `HIGH CPU/QUEUE`.
raj: on it, looking at autoscaler logs and ASG activity. assigning to @eng-oncall. can someone confirm whether new nodegroups were attempted?
ops-bot: Cluster-autoscaler event: Failed to launch node: launch-spec mismatch for nodegroup 'gpu-pool-2', instance profile not found: arn:aws:iam::111222333:instance-profile/redwood-gpu-attach. Error surfaced at 08:04 UTC.
sam: seeing repeated error: "AttachInstanceProfile: NoSuchEntity" in cloudprovider logs. launch-spec refs instance profile name that doesn't exist in this account region after last config rollout.
lucy: that aligns with the deploy yesterday that renamed instance profiles. we probably rolled a launch-spec that still points to the old name. digging.
michelle: customer-impact: multiple customers report increased latency and partial failures for batch embedding jobs. CS is triaging high-volume customers and notifying those with SLA alerts. @customer-success please list affected accounts.
customer-success: early list: acme-ai (elevated errors), atlas-saas (delays), 3 trial accounts hit hard. outreach in progress, will paste updates.
raj: quick mitigation plan: 1) stop new routing to GPU pool (edge policy) 2) manually scale a spare nodegroup with a compatible instance profile 3) patch cluster-autoscaler to ignore broken nodegroup temporarily 4) fallback route requests to smaller-model fleet.
sam: manual scale: creating nodegroup 'gpu-pool-temp' with correct instance profile 'redwood-gpu-attach-v2' and matching taints/labels. will attach to same k8s nodepool. launching now.
lucy: note: launch-spec also had an extra taint key `dedicated=redwood:NoSchedule` that new pool doesn't have. cluster-autoscaler expects taint config; I'll add taint to temp pool to accept workloads.
eng-oncall: patching cluster-autoscaler to skip nodegroup 'gpu-pool-2' until we confirm fix. command:
```
kubectl -n kube-system patch deployment cluster-autoscaler --type json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"EXCLUDE_NG","value":"gpu-pool-2"}}]'
```
ops-bot: autoscaler now reporting: "nodegroup gpu-pool-2 excluded by operator override" at 08:12 UTC.
sam: new nodegroup 'gpu-pool-temp' registered to k8s and nodes are Ready but kubelet reports taint mismatch until I apply taint. applying:
```
kubectl taint nodes node-xyz dedicated=redwood:NoSchedule- || true
kubectl taint nodes node-xyz dedicated=redwood:NoSchedule:NoSchedule
```
michelle: routing rules updated to send new requests to fallback model fleet and to the temporary GPU nodes for canary traffic. reduced token concurrency per-request temporarily (rate limit bumpdown) to protect the pool.
raj: cluster-autoscaler logs show successful scale-up of 'gpu-pool-temp' and now we have ~120 GPUs available. queue decreasing to 4.2k. token 429s dropping.
lucy: root cause summary so far: rollout updated launch-spec/launch-template to reference renamed instance profile and removed taint key. CA could not create nodes for that nodegroup and bubbled up failures. also a missing validation in our rollout pipeline allowed the misaligned spec to ship.
michelle: next steps: 1) reconcile launch-spec names and restore or alias the old instance-profile name (short-term) 2) roll a corrected launch-spec (long-term) 3) add deploy-time validation to catch missing instance profiles and taint mismatches 4) run a capacity soak on the temp pool.
eng-oncall: handing off to night on-call (raj -> lucy) at 09:00 UTC. lucy please keep monitoring queue and confirm CS inbound updates.
raj: leaving notes: temp nodegroup will be left autoscalable, but gpu-pool-2 remains excluded. created runbook section: "temp-nodegroup-creation" and manual rollback commands. log ref: /incidents/3100001234/logs.
customer-success: outreach update: notified acme-ai & atlas-saas, offering credits for errors and live ETA for remediation. both acknowledged and asked for status pings every 30m.
michelle: mitigation status: partial mitigation successful. main risk: if another rollout pushes incompatible launch-specs, we must block until validations are in place. we'll schedule postmortem and include timeline.
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged, P0 -> P1 (partial mitigation). Please submit postmortem within 48h.
lucy: I'll own the postmortem and runbook updates. adding owners: michelle (incident lead), raj (infra root cause), sam (nodegroup ops), lucy (postmortem + rollout validation), customer-success (customer comms).
sam: before I sign off, note a manual workaround: if you see "AttachInstanceProfile: NoSuchEntity" you can temporarily create an alias profile with the old name pointing to the same role to unblock CA while a proper rollout is prepared.
eng-oncall: handoff complete. last check: queue 3.9k, 200 requests/s throttled to 20rps. leaving monitoring alarms at default.
michelle: thanks team. we'll follow up with a full summary and timeline. closing channel for new inputs until postmortem draft.
